_comment: The flash CRC-32 task (issue #20, brief F3, 2026-09-22).
`flash_crc_task` (0x11CB10) is the classic VW Flash-Pruefsumme: a
four-state machine, driven at 0x64 bytes per activation, that hashes the
three ranges of `tbl_crc32_ranges` (0x0A3A10) --
bytes -- with one reflected CRC-32 (polynomial 0xEDB88320) and publishes
the result to RAM.  `re/findings/flash_programming.md` section 5.3a: the
value is REPORTED, never compared, so it cannot stop the engine.  Reading
it is how you tell, over OBD alone, that the flash content changed.
python3 logging/med9log.py log --session logging/sessions/flash_crc.json \
--bus gs_usb:0 --seconds 300 -o logs/2026-xx-xx_flash_crc.csv
Against the simulator (24,627 activations in 4,926 background loops;
246 simulated s at the default T_bg, so give it the time or --time-scale):
python3 logging/ecu_sim.py --bus slcan:/dev/tty.usbmodemXXXX --flash-crc
python3 logging/ecu_sim.py ... --flash-crc 5      # T_bg = 5 ms, 24.6 s
python3 logging/ecu_sim.py ... --flash-crc-warm   # item 1: already done
python3 logging/ecu_sim.py --print-flash-crc --sim-patch patches/ff_fuel
THE PERIOD (G3 2026-09-23, applied by G5 2026-09-24; re/findings/boot.md
6.8 and 6.5(d), scheduler.md 13).  The task is NOT a raster.  Its five
thunks (init-array slots 775-779) are processes of task 0, the set-A
background task, which runs its 13 processes back to back and
re-activates itself at its tail (bg_task_tail 0x11DA64).  So:
* one background loop T_bg = 5 activations = 500 bytes: the cursor
0x7FB700 moves by 0x1F4 per loop (not 0x64 per 10 ms), and the loop
counter bg_loop_count 0x7FD70C moves by 1 per loop;
* the value appears in loop ceil(24,627 / 5) = 4,926, i.e.
t_publish = 4,926 x T_bg after os_init;
* T_bg is bounded 0.51 ms <= T_bg <= 300.75 ms, VERIFIED-STATIC: the
floor is 28,560 emulated instructions per loop at one per 56 MHz
clock, the ceiling is deadline timer 1 (0x100FD7 ticks, expiry is
fatal code 0x74).  So a set-A ECU that keeps running publishes
between 2.5 s and 1,481 s (24.7 min) after power-on;
* the simulator's default T_bg = 50 ms (246 s) is a HYPOTHESIS inside
that bound -- it is what --flash-crc always did.  Where a real ECU
sits is its idle time, a BENCH value.
THE BENCH READ THAT CLOSES IT: log this file (DDLI 2C F0 03 in session
0x89 reads 0x7FB700 and 0x7FD70C) twice -- key on, engine off, and at
idle -- for ~30 s each after a power cycle, and fit
T_bg = 500 bytes / slope(flash_crc_cursor)     [bytes per s]
T_bg = 1 / slope(bg_loop_count)                [counts per s]
The two must agree; bg_loop_count keeps counting after state 7, so it
also works on a warm ECU.  A third, coarser read: t(first pub_hi != 0)
/ 4,926.  Expect T_bg to differ between engine-off and idle.
What to expect, in order:
1. flash_crc_state walks 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 7 and stays at 7.  On a warm
ECU it is already 7 and nothing moves: the task runs ONCE per power
cycle (state 7 sets bit 0 of 0x801200, and the first line of the task
returns on that bit).  Power-cycle before logging.
2. flash_crc_cursor rises monotonically through the three ranges, and
flash_crc_range steps 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 as it crosses them.  Together
they are the progress bar: 0x64 bytes per activation, five
activations = 500 bytes per background loop (see THE PERIOD).
3. flash_crc_acc is the running CRC register (initialised to
0xFFFFFFFF, no reset between ranges, final ^0xFFFFFFFF at the end).
It changes every activation -- it is the only cell that does.
4. flash_crc_pub_hi / _pub_lo stay 0 until state 2, then take the value
ONCE.  0x7F9178 is the HIGH halfword and 0x7F917A the low one
(flash_programming.md 5.3 has them the other way round; brief F3
corrected it from a run).  flash_crc_done goes to 1 with them.
5. For the STOCK image `data/passat_azx_ori.bin` the value is
**0x5562139F** -- pub_hi = 0x5562, pub_lo = 0x139F.  That is
VERIFIED-DYNAMIC from the firmware's own state machine under
emu/ and independently VERIFIED-STATIC from a zlib CRC-32 over the
same three ranges of the dump.  A different value on a car that is
supposed to be stock means the flash content is not this dump.
6. After Flash 1 (patches/ff_counter) or Flash 0 (patches/ff_fuel) the
value MUST change -- the patch blob and both hook words are inside
the hashed ranges.  Recompute the expected value from the patched
image the same way before the bench run, and compare; it is a second,
independent read-back of what was actually programmed, next to
re/findings/flash_programming.md section 7.2's upload of
0x404000-0x47FFFF.  `ecu_sim.py --print-flash-crc --sim-patch DIR`
prints that recomputation (FlashCrcTask.expected, checked against
the firmware's own state machine over ff_fuel's patched tail in
tests/test_ecu_sim_flashcrc.py).  At integration/wave-G (G5,
2026-09-24) it gave 0x32AA60C4 for ff_fuel and 0x06C08AD4 for
ff_counter -- recompute for the exact image you flash; every
FFCAL001 change moves it.
The engine-speed gate: the task's second instruction reads nmot_w
(0x7FEE74) and returns without doing anything while it is >= 0xFFFF, so
the raster counters and nmot_w are logged beside it.

vars.name: flash_crc_state
vars.notes: 0 build the CRC-32 table at 0x800288, 1 hashing, 2 publish, 7 done

vars.name: flash_crc_range
vars.notes: index into tbl_crc32_ranges (0x0A3A10); 3 = past the last range

vars.name: flash_crc_budget
vars.notes: bytes left in this activation; reloaded to 0x64 = 100 each time

vars.name: flash_crc_acc
vars.notes: the running CRC-32 register; 0xFFFFFFFF at the start, inverted once at the end. The only cell that moves every activation

vars.name: flash_crc_end
vars.notes: last address of the range being hashed

vars.name: flash_crc_cursor
vars.notes: next address to hash; the progress bar, +100 per activation = +500 per background loop (G3/G5). T_bg = 500 / slope

vars.name: flash_crc_pub_hi
vars.notes: HIGH halfword of the published CRC; 0x5562 for the stock dump

vars.name: flash_crc_pub_lo
vars.notes: low halfword; 0x139F for the stock dump

vars.name: flash_crc_flags
vars.notes: bit 0 set together with the published value

vars.name: flash_crc_done
vars.notes: bit 0 = the task has published and every later activation returns at once. flash_crc_init (init entry 75) clears it

vars.name: bg_loop_count
vars.notes: one per background loop of task 0; T_bg = 1 / slope. Keeps counting after state 7, so it reads T_bg on a warm ECU too

vars.name: nmot_w
vars.notes: the task's own gate: it returns without work while this word is >= 0xFFFF

vars.name: raster_setA_10ms_count
vars.notes: the ECU clock to fit the activation rate against
